extraction.name: CT-RATE
extraction.description: CT-RATE is a public dataset that pairs 3D medical images with corresponding textual reports. It comprises 25,692 non-contrast 3D chest CT scans from 21,304 unique patients, with each scan accompanied by its corresponding radiology report.
extraction.creator: Ibrahim Ethem Hamamci, Sezgin Er, Chenyu Wang, Furkan Almas, Ayse Gulnihan Simsek, Sewal Nil Esirgun, Irem Dogan, Omer Faruk Durugol, Benjamin Hou, Suprosanna Shit, Weicheng Dai, Murong Xu, Hadrien Reynaud, Muhammed Furkan Dasdelen, Bastian Wittmann, Tamaz Amiranashvili, Enis Simsar, Mehmet Simsar, Emine Bensu Erdemir, Abdullah Alanbay, Anjany Sekuboyina, Berkan Lafci, Ahmet Kaplan, Zhiyong Lu, Malgorzata Polacin, Bemhard Kainz, Christian Bluethgen, Kayhan Batmanghelich, Mehmet Kemal Ozdemir, and Bjoem Menze
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset consists of chest CT volumes and corresponding radiology text reports collected from the Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital database. Every reconstructed non-contrast chest CT volume acquired during the timeframe was incorporated to facilitate a thorough evaluation of various abnormalities.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital database
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Reports were anonymized by removing all personal information pertaining to patients and medical professionals using regular expressions. Anonymized reports were translated from Turkish to English using the Google Translate API, and bilingual final-year medical students reviewed and corrected all translations. For CT volumes, quality control measures excluded volumes involving contrast material or body parts other than the chest. Metadata was also anonymized.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Each CT volume was resized to achieve uniform spacing of 0.75 mm in the x-axis and y-axis and 1.5 mm in the z-axis. Volumes were center-cropped or padded to a consistent resolution of 480x480x240. CT volumes were converted to Hounsfield Unit (HU) values, clipped to a range of -1000 to 1000, and normalized to a range of -1 to 1 during training.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: 1,000 reports were manually annotated by merging findings and impression sections to create a multi-label dataset identifying 18 distinct abnormalities. Conditions not referenced were considered absent, and similar conditions were grouped. This manually annotated set was used to finetune a RadBERT-RoBERTa-4m model, which then automatically classified the remaining 24,692 reports.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: RadBERT-RoBERTa-4m model (for automated report labeling), Llama 3.1 8B (for VQA dataset generation), TotalSegmentator (for 3D nodule segmentation)
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset and models have the potential to efficiently identify pathologies, reduce the workload on radiologists, and potentially save lives in situations where immediate radiological expertise is not available, laying the groundwork for improved patient care.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Biases inherent to the single-institution dataset may influence self-supervised training. The data originates from a single geographic and clinical setting, which may limit the generalizability of the models to other populations.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limitations include potential biases from a single-institution dataset limiting generalizability, dependence on specific terminology used in reports and prompt choices during zero-shot detection, lack of pretrained 3D medical multimodal AI assistants for benchmarking, and the models being strictly limited to chest CT volumes.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Validation, Fine Tuning, zero-shot multi-abnormality detection, volume-to-volume retrieval, report-to-volume retrieval, and visual question-answering (VQA) including radiology report generation.
